approaches.name: Check every pair
approaches.intuition: The answer is one pair of positions, so try them all and stop at the first pair that sums to the target.
steps: For `i` from the first position to the second to last
approaches.time: O(n^2): every pair is looked at once
pitfalls: Using the same position twice: start `j` at `i + 1`.

approaches.name: Hash map of seen values
approaches.intuition: When you reach `x`, the partner you need is `target - x`. If you remember every earlier value and its position, finding that partner is one lookup.
steps: Scan left to right keeping a map from value to position
Return the stored position and the current one
pitfalls: Insert after the lookup, otherwise a value can pair with itself.
Repeated values are fine: the earlier position is found first.

talkTrackMd: Start with the pair check to show the baseline, then say: the slow part is searching for the partner, and a hash map turns that search into a lookup. Mention that you insert after looking up so one element is never used twice.
